program_name: Solar Photovoltaic Program - Residential Option (2026)

program_name: Solar Photovoltaic Program - Commercial Option (2026)
incentive_structure: upfront incentive to service provider from TRM/PVWatts kW and kWh savings; capped at 50% of project cost

program_name: Distributed Generation Interconnection (DG Interconnection Portal) - surplus generation reported to REP
incentive_structure: TDU interconnection only; no TDU export payment

program_name: Commercial Load Management Standard Offer Program (CLM)

incentive_structure: TDU interconnection and DG metering only

program_name: Aggregate Distributed Energy Resource (ADER) Pilot Project - Phase 3.3 (statewide, competitive-area customers via LSE-affiliated or third-party QSE)
incentive_structure: ADER earns ERCOT energy (SCED) and ancillary service (Non-Spin, ECRS) revenue through its QSE; the aggregator/REP sets the customer payment (e.g. Tesla Electric pays a monthly per-Powerwall VPP bill credit plus sellback credits for exported energy)
incentive_value_usd: No ERCOT-set customer payment. Participation limits from 2026-03-02: registered capacity 500 MW (was 200 MW Oct 2025, 160 MW at Phase 3 start), ancillary services 100 MW, single-QSE limit 90%. Oct 2025: 6 ADERs participating, 64.7 MW energy / 40.7 MW Non-Spin / 41.5 MW ECRS, mainly batteries
event_limits: Dispatched via SCED and AS deployments by ERCOT; two models: Aggregate Load Resource (QSE of the customer's LSE) and Phase 3 Aggregate NCLR (third-party QSE may aggregate premises >100 kW with LSE acknowledgment); device-level telemetry validation; each ADER must register with PUCT (Project 54311)
tariff_schedule: ADER Pilot Project Governing Document Phase 3.3; PUCT Project 53911
stackable_with: Customers may not also be in a conflicting ERCOT or utility DR program (e.g. TDU load management SOPs, ERS)

program_name: Emergency Response Service (ERS) - ERS-10 and ERS-30, loads/aggregated loads and non-registered generators
incentive_structure: capacity payment to the QSE for availability per ERS time period, as-bid or market-clearing, reduced for poor availability or performance; QSE/aggregator passes value to customers under its own contract
incentive_value_usd: ERCOT ERS spending capped at $75 million per 12 months (+ up to $25 million for renewals after exhaustion); clearing prices published per term in ERS Procurement Results report
event_limits: 4 standard contract terms (Dec-Mar, Apr-May, Jun-Sep, Oct-Nov); 10- or 30-minute response; deployed to prevent/alleviate EEA (when PRC < 3,000 MW); max 24 cumulative deployment hours per contract period unless renewed; 11 deployments 2007-2025
tariff_schedule: PUCT Subst. R. 25.507; ERCOT Nodal Protocols 3.14.3
stackable_with: Resource cannot be separately obligated for the same capacity in the same hours; excluded from TDU load management SOPs and REP responsive device programs

program_name: Responsive Device Program - Goal for Average Total Residential Load Reduction (SB 1699 / PURA 39.919, 16 TAC 25.186)
incentive_structure: REP (optionally via a demand response provider) may offer residential customers an incentive for smart-device load reduction; REP-set, not a mandated payment
incentive_value_usd: No statutory customer payment. Goal ratio 0.25 load reduction by participating residential customers during ERCOT daily net-load peak; TDUs may use up to 10% of their EE demand-response budget to fund REP responsive device programs
event_limits: must allow summer and winter participation and respond to ERCOT EEAs; must protect critical care/chronic condition customers; enrollment ends with REP contract or when REP is no longer REP of record; REPs report ESI IDs and event times to ERCOT quarterly
stackable_with: Not allowed with ERS or a TDU load management program (25.181-183)

program_name: Residential Demand Response (RDR) Program - NPRR 1296 (proposed ERCOT payment to REPs/NOIEs)
incentive_structure: proposed voluntary pay-for-performance payment from ERCOT to REPs/NOIEs (via QSEs) measured on a high-x-of-y seasonal net-load basis; REP sets the customer incentive
incentive_value_usd: proposed 500 MW seasonal cost cap/target; no rate adopted
event_limits: targets highest seasonal net-load hours
tariff_schedule: NPRR 1296 (tabled at PRS 2025-09-17; pending as of Jul 2026)

program_name: Texas Backup Power Package (TBPP) Program - Texas Energy Fund (critical facilities)
incentive_structure: grants plus forgivable low-cost loans for design, procurement, installation and operation of behind-the-meter backup power packages
incentive_value_usd: $1.8 billion set aside within the $10 billion Texas Energy Fund; grants up to $500/kW plus forgivable loans (per TXSES summary of proposed rule)
event_limits: package must run at least 48 continuous hours without refueling/recharging; must combine natural gas or propane generation, battery storage and solar; facility <2.5 MW; may not sell energy to the grid; eligible hosts limited to critical facilities (hospitals, nursing/assisted living, police/fire, 9-1-1, shelters, water/wastewater, rural fuel stations); rule adopted 2026-05-07, applications expected late 2026/2027
tariff_schedule: PUCT Project 59024; PURA Ch. 34 (Texas Energy Fund)
export_compensation: no export sales allowed from TBPP
stackable_with: Unclear whether TBPP may be used for peak shaving or VPP/ADER participation

program_name: No statewide net metering - export compensation set by retail electric provider in competitive areas
incentive_structure: REP-set buyback (not required by law); TDUs provide interconnection and in/out-flow metering only
export_compensation: REP is not required to credit or buy back out-flows and the value is not set by law or regulation; customer must have in-flow/out-flow metering to be credited
